report: Read all 25 candidate lemmas. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently in a context the source licenses: suffix him/his/it/their/of them (rules 18, 19); waw And/But/who (rules 14, 17 — v0 'who' is a waw + wayyiqtol recast as a relative, v7 keeps its 'And'); מִן from/out of; ל unrepresented after סָבִיב in v7 (rule 40, 'round about' whole to the adverb) but 'to' in v9 where the ASV writes it; ל of לְדָוִד 'of' in v0 but nothing before the bare object of 'magnify' in v3; article 'the' in v8, nothing under 'What man' in v12, 'he that'/'them that' where rendered substantivally (rule 41). No split found.

Read the eight added units end to end, since the table is blind to them: 'A Psalm' (v0), 'thereof' (v2), 'him' after שָׁמֵעַ (v6), the relative 'that' over יֶחֱסֶה־בּוֹ (v8), 'And' before אֹהֵב with no waw (v12), italic 'open' (v15), italic 'The righteous' (v17), 'He' before שֹׁמֵר (v20, no nominal in the verse). Each is the contract's own case; v6 and v17 are the same verb with and without a supplied object and are treated consistently under rule 44.
BSB disagreements (3) are all documented convention, none an error: v3 לַ before a bare English object, v7 לִ after 'round about' (rule 40), v12 הָ of הָאִישׁ under 'What man'.

Two hedged readings stand with their competing reading named in the note and need no patch: v12 'he that' given to the article on חָפֵץ under rule 41 (alternative: cleft 'he' added under rule 20); v22 the chain's 'of' on the participle rather than on the article's 'them that' unit.

v11 'Come ye children' is a genuine tie under rule 36 — the 'ye' stands both after the imperative and before the vocative noun. The verse pass gave it to the noun, which the ASV's own punctuation ('Come, ye children,') supports; left as is, not promoted, since the token stream carries no punctuation for a rule to read.
The eight repeated notes the validator lists (rules 16, 17, 20, 29, 46) restate contract rules and are not recorded as conventions.
